explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/397: 'Are there only finitely many solutions to ∏_i C(2m_i, m_i) = ∏_j C(2n_j, n_j) with the m_i, n_j distinct?', answered negatively (Somani's family with c = 8a²+8a+1). The Lean statement asserts that the set of pairs of disjoint finsets (M, N) of naturals with ∏_{i∈M} centralBinom i = ∏_{j∈N} centralBinom j is infinite. Finsets make the m_i (and the n_j) distinct, and disjointness makes all of them distinct. Degenerate solutions do not trivialise the claim: centralBinom 0 = 1 and empty products only produce finitely many extra solutions from any given one (adding or removing 0), so the Lean set is infinite iff there are infinitely many genuine solutions with positive entries. Faithful.
